verdict.rationale: WorkOS ships a first-party remote MCP server that lets MCP-compatible AI agents read and change the same dashboard data a user can, including organizations, connections, users and branding. That makes natural-language operation possible, but only through an external agent acting as the MCP client; the evidence shows no built-in natural-language console or assistant. Missing for 10: a native in-product natural-language command interface, documentation of which operations the MCP server covers and their limits, and independent or hands-on evidence of NL-driven operation working in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: The WorkOS MCP server is a remote management Model Context Protocol server that lets MCP-compatible AI agents act on your WorkOS workspace.
Once connected, your agent can read and change the same dashboard data you can (managing organizations, connections, users, branding, and more) by calling the WorkOS API on your behalf.
